headline: Volume softness and Argo disruption compress margins
summary_short: Ingredion's Q1 2026 net sales were $1,792M (-1.2% y/y), but net income fell 27.9% y/y to $142M ($2.22 diluted EPS) as gross margin compressed to 22% from 26% on lower volumes and an Argo, Illinois production disruption.
summary_long: Net sales dipped 1.2% y/y to $1,792M as lower volume/mix in F&II-U.S./Canada (-9% segment sales) outweighed T&HS growth (+2.5%) and favorable FX. Gross margin fell to 22% from 26% y/y on lower fixed-cost absorption; F&II-U.S./Canada operating income dropped 63% y/y on Argo facility production challenges plus softer volumes/mix. F&II-LATAM operating income fell 9% y/y on Mexico currency impacts. Operating cash flow nearly halved to $33M y/y on the net income decline. Capex rose to $110M; management guides remainder-of-2026 capex to $400-440M. Cash fell to $914M q/q after $52M dividends and capex. Subsequent to quarter-end: a ~$43M Cabo, Brazil closure charge and ~$20M Argo thermal-event cost, both expected in Q2 2026.

drivers.explanation: Decrease driven primarily by lower volume and less favorable mix in F&II-U.S./Canada, partially offset by higher T&HS net sales and favorable FX.
Gross margin fell to 22% from 26% primarily from lower fixed-cost absorption tied to lower volumes; cost of sales itself rose on increased F&II-U.S./Canada operating costs.
Decline reflects lower gross profit and increased operating expenses (the latter driven by higher employee costs) plus higher restructuring/impairment charges tied to legal-entity restructuring.
Decrease was primarily due to the decline in operating income, partially offset by a lower income-tax provision.
Decline primarily attributable to a $55M decrease in net income, partly offset by a $26M working-capital change driven by decreased inventories.
Higher spend to update, expand and improve facilities versus the prior-year quarter; no further breakdown given.

F&II-U.S./Canada segment operating income fell 63% y/y on production challenges at the Argo facility and softer volumes/mix -- the single largest driver of the consolidated operating-income decline; F&II-LATAM operating income also fell 9% on Mexico transactional currency impacts, partially offset by a roughly flat T&HS segment.
